title: Do the three expressions for the slanting region match?
description: A region with slanting lines is measured three ways: a big square take away a rectangle, a long rectangle take away three rectangles, and two times a thin rectangle. Each expression is multiplied out to show they are the same, and then the area is found for x as eight and y as three. Keeko doubts that expressions which look different can give one area.
teaching_notes: One idea: different looking expressions for one region are equal, and multiplying them out shows it. Watch for students who think three different looking expressions must give three different areas.

source: Verify that x² − xy, x(x + 2y) − 3xy and x(x − y) are equal,
video_script.why: The child has matched two areas by multiplying out, and now matches three areas of one region found by three different cuts.
video_script.substitution: Write each child's area, multiply it out to x squared minus x y, and put in x as eight and y as three.
video_script.anchor: the region with slanting lines among three equal rectangles, each with sides x and y
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks three expressions that look different must give three different areas, though all three describe the same region.
video_script.payoff_line: All three expressions equal x squared minus x y, and the area is forty square units

final_answer.value: All three equal x² − xy; the area is 40 square units
final_answer.spoken: all three equal x squared minus x y; the area is forty square units

names.{{NAME_3}}: finds the slanted region's area as a big square minus one rectangle
names.{{NAME_4}}: finds the slanted region's area as a long rectangle minus three rectangles
names.{{NAME_5}}: finds the slanted region's area as twice one rectangle

never_show: three different areas marked as right
maths_rules: each of the three equal rectangles has sides x and y, so area xy
first method: big square x² minus one rectangle xy, so x² − xy
second method: the long rectangle has side y + x + y = x + 2y and side x, so area x(x + 2y), and x(x + 2y) − 3xy
x(x + 2y) = x × x + x × 2y = x² + 2xy, and x² + 2xy − 3xy = x² − xy
third method: two times a rectangle with sides (x − y)/2 and x, so 2 × x × (x − y)/2 = x(x − y)
x(x − y) = x × x − x × y = x² − xy
video_script.design: One idea: one region has one area, so expressions that describe it are equal. Wrong idea: different looking expressions give different areas. The figure stays all video; the working board holds the three expressions.

<bookmark mark='mul'/>Multiply out to get x times x, plus x times two y, take away three x y.
<bookmark mark='join'/>Two x y take away three x y is minus x y. The area is x squared minus x y.

<bookmark mark='mul'/>Multiply out to get x times x, take away x times y. That is x squared minus x y.
